incidents.vector: Suspected hack of the exchange's infrastructure or hot wallets; technical details not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Up to $5.5 billion in cryptocurrency stolen, with roughly $1.8 billion frozen by Tether and Circle but at least $1.2 billion in USDT and ETH still in the attacker's control, making it the largest crypto heist on record.

incidents.victim: Zenith Technology (New Zealand clinical trial/lab services)
incidents.vector: Zawoo ransomware attack on a private company providing clinical trial and analytical laboratory services.
incidents.impact: Delayed lab work for New Zealand patients and, as a downstream effect, delayed coronial autopsy investigations across the country.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached an Okta single sign-on database used by DHS and obtained internal personnel records dating back to 2011; Okta says its own systems were not compromised.
incidents.impact: Personal data on more than 41,000 DHS employees and contractors, including ICE and CBP staff, was published via a searchable "Icepick" archive hosted by DDoSecrets; takedown attempts by a DHS contractor have so far failed to keep it offline.

incidents.victim: Multiple foreign ministries, defense/semiconductor/pharma firms, and telecom providers (14+ countries)
incidents.vector: AI-driven agentic penetration-testing framework run on Chinese-developed and commercial LLMs, used to chain exploits (SAML/XXE, orchestration-service abuse, stolen VPN/mail keys) against foreign ministries, defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor and telecom targets in parallel.
incidents.impact: More than 200 organizations targeted since Oct. 17 across Latin America, Europe, Asia, the Middle East and the U.S.; confirmed post-exploitation (BLOODALCHEMY backdoor, credential spraying, domain admin recovery) at nine organizations.

incidents.victim: GMO Internet (Onamae Desktop Cloud / FX trading service)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to GMO's Onamae Desktop Cloud service hosting its FX foreign-exchange trading platform.
incidents.impact: Attackers demanded a $50 million ransom and leaked some stolen data on the dark web; GMO is offering a $1 million reward for information on the hackers.

incidents.victim: Multiple space/satellite, defense, aerospace and policy-research organizations
incidents.vector: Exploited CVE-2026-20127, an authentication bypass in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller instances, to deploy a custom malware framework for long-term control-plane access and encryption-key theft.
incidents.impact: Persistent access and exfiltration of sensitive keying material from affected Cisco SD-WAN environments; infrastructure overlaps with a known China state-linked covert access network.

incidents.vector: Breach at Amadeus IT Group, the third-party provider running JAL's flight reservation, ticketing and check-in systems.
incidents.impact: Reservation data for roughly 92,000 Japan Airlines and Japan Transocean Air customers exposed; about 2,000 customers also had passport numbers, frequent-flyer numbers, emails and phone numbers stolen. Flight operations and payment card data were not affected.

incidents.victim: 47 Western media entities, businesses, NGOs and government entities (historical, 2011-2024)
incidents.vector: Hacking conspiracy organized by members of the former Assad regime's inner circle, including spear-phishing and social media account takeovers, conducted over more than a decade.
incidents.impact: Ahmad Umar Agha ("Th3Pr0") sentenced to 42 months for hacks that included a fake tweet causing a temporary $136 billion flash crash in Dow Jones stocks and redirecting the U.S. Marine Corps recruitment site; case resolved after Agha spent a decade as a fugitive.

incidents.vector: Intrusion detected in the FEC's electronic campaign-finance filing system; technical details not disclosed.
incidents.impact: FEC shut down its electronic filing system, used to track political-party spending, one week before the U.S. midterm elections; the agency says voting operations are unaffected.

incidents.vector: Destructive data-wiping malware deployed by a Belarusian state-linked group (tracked by ESET as "FrostyNeighbor"/GhostWriter), acting as a cyber-proxy for Russian intelligence priorities in Ukraine.
incidents.impact: First-ever documented destructive wiper attack attributed to a Belarusian state actor, marking an operational escalation; Belarus becomes the sixth state ever publicly documented deploying wiper malware.

incidents.vector: DPRK IT workers use fraudulent documents, stolen identities and fabricated personas, aided by AI tools, to secure remote employment at U.S. and allied companies, then exploit their corporate network access.
incidents.impact: OFAC sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity (facilitators in Russia and North Korea) for laundering and transferring revenue from the scheme; DPRK IT workers have also used their network access to deploy malware, exfiltrate sensitive data and steal proprietary information from victim companies.

incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Health System
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack by a new gang calling itself "BYOD" against UNM's Health Sciences Center systems.
incidents.impact: Ambulances diverted to other hospitals, dozens of outpatient surgeries and appointments canceled, and medical school classes disrupted for several days; no ransom paid. Attackers also stole patient and employee data and threatened to retain it.

incidents.victim: U.S. government-affiliated organization (via Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewalls)
incidents.vector: Chained the "PHP2Shell" PHP core RCE flaws (CVE-2026-109618/109619) with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation bug (CVE-2026-46300) against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces, using Chinese-language tooling, FOFA reconnaissance and Claude Code/DeepSeek/Kimi AI tools to narrow roughly 19,000 exposed firewalls down to a 240-target list.
incidents.impact: 24 firewalls compromised; two servers at a U.S. government-affiliated environment were fully breached, giving the attacker likely persistent access, a full Active Directory blueprint, credentials and network topology. Palo Alto Networks independently confirmed the campaign.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of unauthenticated vulnerabilities in a government logging service, then pivoting through interconnected government systems to make roughly 11 million data-extraction requests.
incidents.impact: Personal data tied to about 750,000 citizens (roughly a third of Moldova's population) exposed, including family, health, financial, and vehicle/business ownership records; 82 digital public services and 30+ government networks were taken offline. Authorities are investigating possible foreign-state involvement.

incidents.vector: Breach of Vanden Broele's eSignFlow document-signing platform used by Belgian local governments.
incidents.impact: More than 120 local Belgian authorities had their document-signing services disrupted after the company proactively took systems offline to prevent abuse.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime and shipping companies
incidents.vector: Supply-chain compromise of maritime IT services provider CyberLogitec, pivoting to downstream port authority, maritime and shipping company customers.
incidents.impact: Ransomware and data-extortion group "n0n" listed 40+ victims on its dark-web leak site; half of the listed companies are known CyberLogitec customers. Payment deadlines expired Oct. 19 with no confirmed payment.

incidents.victim: Multiple Starlink satellite internet customers (100+ countries)
incidents.vector: Israeli advertising company Discover-Tech served as the top bidder for ad space targeting Starlink users, using those ads to deliver zero-click spyware.
incidents.impact: Zero-click spyware delivered to Starlink customers across more than 100 countries, including countries where Starlink service is banned or restricted, enabling likely surveillance of targeted individuals.

incidents.vector: N/A — law enforcement action: FBI and federal prosecutors obtained a court order to seize the domain of Virtualine, a Russian-speaking bulletproof hosting provider.
incidents.impact: Disrupted hosting infrastructure used for sextortion schemes, ransomware, data theft, malware distribution, money laundering and CSAM; Virtualine received nearly one-fifth of all illicit-attributed cryptocurrency inflow among tracked bulletproof hosts in 2026. Underlying operators are not confirmed to have stopped operating.

incidents.vector: Breach of a university test environment.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 525,000 people stolen.

incidents.vector: Third party misused the company's member information retrieval API.
incidents.impact: 22,519,960 customer records compromised, including email addresses, passwords, names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth and employment information.

incidents.vector: Breach of Coinbase's third-party analytics provider, Amplitude.
incidents.impact: Some customer data stolen; Coinbase says the incident was limited to data accessible through the analytics integration.

incidents.vector: AI-assisted attacks using an open-source agentic penetration-testing framework, run with multiple commercial AI assistants, opportunistically testing for weaknesses across multiple financial institutions.
incidents.impact: Personal data belonging to at least 68,000 people exposed across at least seven South Korean financial institutions; one breach exposed an outsourced developer's data, another resulted in customer data theft.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack against Japanese cloud hosting provider IDCFrontier.
incidents.impact: Disrupted services for 495 downstream companies and local governments relying on IDCFrontier's cloud infrastructure.
